🍁With trade tensions heating back up — Trump has vowed a fresh 50% tariff on some Canadian goods, invoking Section 338 of the 1930 Tariff Act (a Depression-era provision never before used for tariffs) to hit ~$20B of imports like milk, beer, hockey equipment and plywood, while sparing energy, potash and critical minerals — here's what the data is actually saying: ☑️ Canada's effective tariff rate sits near 3.1% — below Mexico's ~3.7%. Yet Canada's imports stalled through the 2025 escalation while Mexico's climbed to a record ~$55B in May. ☑️ Since 2016, Mexico is up ~140% vs Canada's ~63%. They started roughly equal — Mexico has pulled decisively ahead. ☑️ Why? Canada's headline number is dominated by energy, which moves on price, not policy.
